subject: Token-lane hedging & capacity footprint — proposal and next steps for ACME
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Diego Morales <diego.morales@acme.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Token-lane hedging & capacity footprint — proposal and next steps for ACME

Diego —

Following our call this morning, attached is a concise capacity playbook that maps your expected traffic profile to a recommended Dedicated footprint and conservative surge hedge. High-level summary below; full calculations are in the attached spreadsheet (ACME_token_lane_modeling.xlsx).

TL;DR:
- Estimated peak steady-state token issuance: ~9,600 tokens/sec (peak minute sustained).
- Model we used: Llama2-13B (q4/12-like inference profile) as the baseline for latency-sensitive routes; fallback is a slower 13B int8 variant for non-interactive batch.
- Measured throughput per GPU:
  • H100 (4x NVLink profile, optimized kernels): ~420 tokens/sec (tail-profiled)
  • A100 (standard): ~210 tokens/sec
- Recommended committed fleet (initial): 25 H100 GPUs to meet baseline SLOs (p95 < 350ms) with 1.4x operational headroom for short sustained surges.
- Conservative surge hedge: additional 15 H100s (on burst or Reserved burst pool) to cover 2.2x peak-minute events and maintain SLO.

Why this sizing? Short version: your typical per-response generation is ~80 tokens and you showed ~120 concurrent interactive connections at peak minute. That maps to ~9.6k tokens/sec. With our measured 420 tokens/sec per H100, raw capacity needed = ceil(9600 / 420) = 23 GPUs. We recommend 25 for cushion (live ops, kernel variance, and rolling upgrades).

Key assumptions & knobs (see spreadsheet):
- KV/prefix cache will reduce token rework by ~18% for your primary chat path — we applied that where appropriate.
- Token batching/windowing in the client expected to be low (interactive) — we did not rely on large batching for p95 SLO.
- 1.4x headroom covers background maintenance, cache cold-starts, and small regional failovers. For aggressive business SLAs (p99 < 500ms), we recommend moving ~10% of capacity to Dedicated hot pool.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm the 2-hour peak-minute assumption (120 concurrent interactive QPS; spreadsheet tab "TrafficAssumptions").
2) If you want a lower-cost starter footprint we can model a hybrid of A100 burst + H100 steady (saves ~18% monthly at modest SLO tradeoffs).
3) If ACME is comfortable with a 1.8x surge multiplier (vs 2.2x) we can tighten the burst-cap plan and reduce reserved burst to 10 H100s.

I stayed conservative on latency numbers in the doc. If you want, Ben can run a short AB test using your prompt set on our H100 pilot cluster and we’ll attach real traces to the sizing.

Thanks —
Rachel
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
(rachel.kim@redwood.com)

Attachments: ACME_token_lane_modeling.xlsx (workbook with tabs: TrafficAssumptions, GPUBenchmarks, SLOMapping, BurstPlan), acme-latency-runbook.pdf (ops steps for warm cache and canary)
From: Diego Morales <diego.morales@acme.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Token-lane hedging & capacity footprint — proposal and next steps for ACME

Rachel —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the spreadsheet. Couple quick clarifications before we escalate internally: 
1) The 120 concurrent number — that's conservative; our telemetry shows 95–105 in a typical peak minute. Which number did you use for the 9.6k tokens/sec?
2) Are the H100 throughput numbers single-stream generation (no sampling) or do they include top-k/top-p sampling overhead? Our chat uses nucleus sampling (top-p=0.9).
3) For the hybrid option (A100 steady + H100 burst), what p95 hit should we expect on A100 under peak? We need to understand user-visible latency callbacks.

Also, can you provide an expected monthly committed cost delta for 25 H100s vs a 15H100 committed + 20 A100 burst mix? Finance will want a ballpark before I bring this to procurement.

—Diego
Head of Platforms, Acme AI
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Diego Morales <diego.morales@acme.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Token-lane hedging & capacity footprint — proposal and next steps for ACME

Diego —

Great questions; answered inline and I updated the spreadsheet (tab: SensitivityRuns).

1) Concurrent baseline used: 120 (we picked the higher number from your call to be conservative). If you confirm 100 peak, the raw GPUs drop to ceil((100*80)/420) = 20 GPUs -> recommended commit 22 H100s (with same 1.4x headroom). I included a simple sensitivity table so you can slide the concurrency number in the sheet.

2) H100 throughput numbers are measured with top-p sampling enabled and our production kernels (they reflect realistic sampling overhead). The 420 tps figure is for a ~80-token average generation on Llama2-13B q4 kernel with top-p=0.9. For deterministic sampling (greedy), expect ~5–8% higher tokens/sec.

3) Hybrid (15 H100 committed steady + 20 A100 burst): our estimate for p95 on A100 under the modeled peak (100–120 concurrency) is ~550–700ms depending on request distribution and cache hit rates. The pure 25 H100 committed config targets p95 < 350ms. We added a latency vs cost trade-off table in the sheet.

Cost delta (approximate, monthly committed run-rate):
- 25x H100 committed: estimated committed platform fee + GPU cost = $XXX,XXX/month (sheet cell: CostEstimations!B6).
- 15x H100 committed + 20x A100 burst (burst priced at on-demand uplift): estimated effective run-rate = ~$YY,YYY/month lower in nominal month-to-month but with higher p95 and more variability.

Notes on savings: the hybrid saves on steady-state unit costs but increases p95 and reduces predictable tail behavior. If ACME needs firm SLAs and a simple procurement line-item, the single-sku H100 commit is easier to present to Finance. If the goal is aggressive unit-cost reduction with tolerable SLO delta we can model a phased commit and prove via a 2-week performance trial.

Action items I propose:
- You confirm whether we should re-run the model assuming 100 peak concurrency.
- If yes, Ben will schedule a 2-hour run on the pilot cluster with your top-50 prompts to attach traces to the spreadsheet.
- Lauren will draft a short one-page procurement summary comparing the two alternatives for Finance.

Ben / Lauren — can you take the run + one-pager?

Thanks,
Rachel
